title: Yochanan Chakuka’ah
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Pesachim 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.13a.11): he came before Rabbi to ask about a bag full of chametz that someone had deposited with him and that mice had pierced, etc. In [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 1:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.1.4.6), the incident is told as follows: a man deposited a bag of chametz with R. Ch. Rabbah; R. Y. bar Bun said, ‘It was Yochanan Chakukya.’ And in [Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 3:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Metzia.3.4.2): Rabbi Yochanan Chakukah deposited chametz with R. Ch. Rubba; he asked Rabbi, etc.[^1]

[Pesachim 3b (Hyman cites 53b)](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.3b.14) relates that he once went out to the villages. They asked him whether the wheat had done well, and he answered that the barley had done well. The reply was, ‘Go and bring the good news to the horses and donkeys.’ There R. Ch. explains that he was a scribe, while R. Y. explains that he was from the town of Chakukah.[^2]

notes.text: The linked Yerushalmi Pesachim has Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Bun name Yochanan Chikukya as the man who deposited bread with Rabbi Chiyya the Elder. In the parallel, he is called Rabbi Yochanan Chakukah and the deposit is chametz. The Bavli has someone else deposit the bag with Yochanan.

[Rabbeinu Chananel](https://www.sefaria.org/Rabbeinu_Chananel_on_Pesachim.3b.6) interprets Chakuka’ah as “scribe.” [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1840&lang=en) cites the wheat and barley story at 3b and records the alternative place-name explanation. Hyman leaves the person who answers about the horses and donkeys unnamed.
